reported for cement, fertilisers and electricity. Iron and steel, aluminium and
hydrogen are direct only during that period. This is one of the most common

Article 18
Reporting obligation during the transitional period
Each reporting declarant shall, for each quarter of a calendar year, submit a
CBAM report containing information on the goods imported during that quarter, no
later than one month after the end of that quarter. The CBAM report shall
contain the total quantity of each type of goods, the total embedded direct
emissions, the total embedded indirect emissions, and the carbon price due in a
country of origin for the embedded emissions, taking into account any rebate or
other form of compensation available.

The following goods are covered: cement; electricity; fertilisers; iron and
steel; aluminium; hydrogen. Indirect emissions are covered for cement,
fertilisers and electricity. For iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen, only
direct emissions are covered during the transitional period. The greenhouse

11 Penalties during the transitional period
If you do not report, or you report something incomplete or incorrect and do not
fix it when asked, the penalty is between EUR 10 and EUR 50 per tonne of
unreported emissions. It goes up if you have submitted more than two bad reports
in a row or if you have not reported for more than six months. The authority
takes into account how much was missing, whether you cooperated, and whether it
was deliberate.

12 Common mistakes
Reporting electricity in tonnes rather than megawatt hours. Assuming the
estimated values published for the transitional period remain available after 31
July 2024. Assuming indirect emissions are reported for iron and steel during
the transitional period, when only direct emissions are. Forgetting that the
EUR 150 threshold is per consignment, not per year.

3 What changes and when
From 1 October 2023 to 31 December 2025 you only report. You do not buy
certificates and you do not pay anything under the mechanism. From 1 January
2026 you must be an authorised declarant before you import, you submit an annual
declaration, and you surrender certificates for the emissions you declared.

4 Quarterly reporting during the transitional period
You submit one report per quarter through the transitional registry, within one
month of the quarter ending. So the report for January to March is due by 30
April. You report how much of each good you imported, where it was made, which
production route was used, and the emissions embedded in it, split into direct
and indirect. You also report any carbon price you already paid in the country
where the goods were made.

surrender certificates, or if you miss the annual declaration deadline two years
running. You get the chance to be heard first and the decision must give
reasons, and it can be appealed.

An authorised CBAM declarant may claim in its CBAM declaration a reduction in

Q6 What is a complex good
A good whose production consumes precursor materials that are themselves covered
goods. Its embedded emissions include the embedded emissions of those
precursors, not only the emissions of the final production process. A simple
good has no such precursors, and its embedded emissions are the attributed
emissions of its own process divided by the activity level.

Q7 We paid a carbon price in the country of production. Does that help
From 2026, yes. You can reduce the number of certificates you surrender by the
carbon price effectively paid for the same emissions, provided no export rebate
or other compensation was available in that country. You need documentation
certified by an independent person. During the transitional period you report
the carbon price due but there is nothing to reduce, because nothing is
surrendered.

Synthetic questions and answers on the mechanism

Q1 Is the mechanism a tax
No. It is not levied at the border as a duty. During the transitional period
nothing is payable at all. From 2026 the importer buys certificates from its
Member State and surrenders them once a year against the emissions it declared,
which is closer to how allowances work under the emissions trading system than
to how a customs duty works.

Q2 We import small quantities. Are we caught
Only if a consignment exceeds EUR 150 in total intrinsic value. The threshold is
per consignment. Splitting a shipment to stay under it is not a strategy anyone
should rely on, and repeated consignments to the same buyer may be looked at
together.
